original_question: For an m-dimensional continued fraction in the geometric sense of the paper, determine which integer n-gons can occur as faces. This includes both faces at integer distance 1 from the origin and faces at integer distance greater than 1 from the origin.
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Problem 5: "Which n-gons are realizable as faces of an m-dimensional continued fraction?" together with its two subcases by integer distance to the origin.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly asks about realizability of integer n-gons as faces of an m-dimensional continued fraction, and it explicitly preserves the paper's two geometrically different subcases: faces at integer distance 1 from the origin and faces at integer distance greater than 1.
missing_details: The paper's exact target is an open problem labeled Problem 5 in Section 3.2, not a theorem or conjecture.

The phrase "m-dimensional continued fraction" should be tied to the paper's notion of a geometric multidimensional continued fraction via sails (Section 2.1, Definition 2.2), with Section 3.2 aimed mostly at the Klein-polyhedron setting.
It helps to state the quantifiers explicitly: the problem is for given integers m >= 2 and n >= 3.
The question is specifically about realizability of integer n-gons as 2-dimensional faces.

The meaning of "integer distance" should be made explicit: it is the paper's lattice-theoretic integer distance from the origin (the cone vertex) to the plane/supporting affine subspace of the face, as defined in Section 1.1.
For the distance-1 case, the paper frames the problem as describing integer convex polygons inscribed in full-dimensional simplices of the ambient lattice space.
For the distance->1 case, the paper frames the problem as a view-obstacle problem, i.e. one must avoid intermediate integer points that obstruct visibility from the origin.

For full paper-faithfulness, one may note the stated status: the triangular case is trivial, and two-dimensional faces at integer distance greater than 1 are already classified; the remaining cases are open.
refined_question: For fixed integers m >= 2 and n >= 3, in the setting of geometric multidimensional continued fractions defined by sails in integer geometry, classify the integer n-gons that are realizable as 2-dimensional faces of an m-dimensional continued fraction, distinguishing the two geometrically different cases according to the integer distance from the supporting plane of the face to the origin (the cone vertex): (i) faces at integer distance 1, i.e. the problem of describing integer convex n-gons that can occur as faces inscribed in full-dimensional simplices of the ambient lattice space; and (ii) faces at integer distance greater than 1, i.e. the corresponding view-obstacle problem in which intervening integer points must be avoided.
justification: The paper is an open-problems note, and your draft clearly matches Section 3.2, Problem 5 almost verbatim. I therefore kept the scope exactly at realizable n-gonal faces, without broadening to the more general face-classification Problem 3 or to empty simplices in Problem 4. I only made explicit the definitions that the paper leaves implicit in the short problem statement: that "continued fraction" means a geometric multidimensional continued fraction defined via sails, that the origin is the cone vertex, that integer distance is the lattice-theoretic notion from Section 1.1, and that the two subcases are precisely the paper's distance-1 and distance->1 formulations.
